en.text:
## Instructions

## 🛑🚫✋ I HIGHLY suggest that you fix the seed, run the pic, then don’t mess with anything before this so it doesn’t reprocess.

### Node order (follow the chain top → bottom)

**Smart Denoise (LCImageDenoise)**  
- Removes noise while trying to keep detail  
- Sigma: higher = smoother, lower = more detail  
- Threshold: how aggressive the denoise is  
- Radius Multiplier: higher for noisy images, lower for clean ones  
💡 Start gentle. Only raise values if the image is actually noisy.

**Color Match (LCColorMatch)**  
- Matches colors to a reference image (usually Image 2)  
- Method: “adain” is the most common and stable  
- Strength: 0–1  

**Sharpen Pro (LCSharpenPro)**  
- Adaptive mid-tone contrast / micro-contrast  
- Radius, strength, blend mode, shadow/highlight controls  
💡 Super important node. Adds “pop” without the cardboard cut-out look.

**Image Adjust (LCImageAdjust)**  
- Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Sharpness, Blur  
- Brightness center = 0  
- Contrast & Saturation center = 1  

**LC Natural Look 🍃**
- Takes the AI look out without making the picture dull.
- Pulls back only the loudest colours, calms orange and plastic skin, rolls the highlights off instead of clipping them, and cuts the glossy glow while lifting fine texture.
- Your black point, contrast and brightness stay where they were, with a whisper of grain on top.
- Goes **last** in post, after the LUT, so the grain sits on top of everything.
- **strength:** 0.3 - 0.6 for most renders.
- **skin:** how much orange / plastic skin is calmed, on top of strength. 0 = skin untouched.


**Apply LUT (LCApplyLUT)**  
- Applies a 3D LUT (.cube file)  
- Strength 0–1  
- Log option for certain LUTs  
💡 Free LUTs at freshluts.com. Strength 0.3–0.7 is often nicer than 1.0. Put .cube files in the luts folder.

nodes.title: 2nd Image 🖼️ & 🙂 Head Swap

en.text:
## Adding a 2nd Image 🖼️🖼️

**As a reference**
- turn on 2nd Image switch
- in general remove the background unless there is no subject
- prompt accordingly. "subject in image 1, subject in image 2, etc."

**For 🙂 Head Swap**
- this will alwaye be hit or miss. Try several different seeds 🌱
- leave the main prompt blank
- Use a clean face reference image. A headshot is best
- ⚠️ Remove background should be on
- Turn on Head Swap prompt
- Set the reference boost all the way to 4, and lower the main one to 1

en.text:
## 📐 Aspect Ratio Simplifier Instructions 

- **Max_resolution** determines how large the overall resolution is. 💡 Set lower for faster generation

- **resolution source**: This uses the aspect ratio of the image 🖼️ , or a custom preset
- **aspect ratio**: Set a custom value or use a preset
- **swap dimensions**: turns the resolution on it's side

nodes.title: ⚙️ Settings

en.text:
### Settings

**Seed**
- this is the value the model uses to choose a noise latent. 
- **💡I always use a fixed seed** (unless I'm experimenting). When I want a change, I'll hit "New Fixed Random". I do this so that I can adjust things without it regenerating and be able to see what the adjustments do.
- everything that uses a seed is tied to this.

**Ksampler Settings**
- **steps total**: number of steps to generate. anywhere between 8-10. It really differs between models
- **refiner_steps**: This is the amount of steps the refiner uses.
- **CFG (Classifier Free Guidance):** 1.0


### Options Switches:
- turns off and on all areas of the workflow without having to manualy bypass them

### Reference Boost
- The standard setting is 1.0, but I've noticed that locks facial expressions
- Balance between Image 1 and Image 2 by using these
   - 1 for both seems to work pretty well. 
- Lower settings mean less attention to the character

### Instructions: 

- Use a simple prompt. "Change her outfit to a red dress", "Put the outfit from image 2 on the woman in image 1"

nodes.title: LC VOSR2 Upscale🧩

en.text:
## LC VOSR2 Upscale🧩

**What is it?**

- An upscaler built for *speed* and low VRAM, with the highest quality possible.

- It uses a dedicated upscale model (VOSR 2.0) that sharpens and adds fine detail without redrawing the picture.

- 💡Hook it up after my detailers with the pipe version. It passes along what the detailers already fixed, so LC Skin Upscale and LC Skin Texture don't turn skin pores into freckles or craters.
---

### Speed and size chart*

| upscale_by | Output size | Time | GPU memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.5x | 1596 x 2028 | 2.8 s | 4.7 GB |
| 2x | 2128 x 2704 | 4.4 s | 4.8 GB |
| 3x | 3192 x 4056 | 8.6 s | 5.1 GB |
| 4x | 4256 x 5408 | 16 s | 5.7 GB |
| 6x (3x + 2x) | 6384 x 8112 | 46 s | 8.4 GB |
| 8x (4x + 2x) | 8512 x 10816 | 75 s | 12.0 GB |

**All tests based on a 1064x1352 render on an RTX 5090, warm.*

**⏱️ Time will vary by card, but the output size will not. About 5 GB covers 1.5x - 3x, so it can almost run on a 🥔**

---

**Settings ⚙️**

- **tile_size:** 512, what it was trained at. Leave it.
- **vae_tile_size:** lower = less VRAM, a little slower.
- **seed:** only changes the finest grain.
- **protected:** the detailers' areas at the new size. Wire it into **protect_mask** on LC Skin Upscale and LC Skin Texture so they do not add skin detail twice.

nodes.title: **LC Smart Detailer 🩹**

en.text:
**LC Smart Detailer 🩹**
- Finds the face with SAM 3, redraws it at full detail, and blends it back in.
- Runs **before** the upscale, on the small picture, where it is fast and sees the whole face.
- **prompt:** "Face". Add **:1** (`Face:1`) for only the biggest face.
- **threshold:** 0.5. Lower finds more (and more wrong things).
- **grow:** 4 - 8. **feather:** 8 - 12.
- **padding:** 64 - 128. More = the model sees more of the scene around the face.
- **inpaint_resolution:** 1024.
- **denoise:** 0.3 - 0.35. Higher starts adding blotches and freckles, then redraws a different face.
- **blend:** 1. Want a lighter touch? Lower the denoise, not the blend.
- **cfg:** 1. **tone_match:** on.
- **inpaint_positive:** leave it empty, the main prompt is used.
- ⚠️ Do not use "detailed realistic skin". In Krea 2 that means "Hey! Make giant pores and blotches!!"

tour.title: ComfyUI Workflow Tour: Lonecat's Krea2 Identity Edit & Head Swap V7.1

steps.title: Load Image 📷
steps.text:
Load the photo you want to edit and set the size here.

💡 Set the max resolution lower for faster generation.

settings.why: Uses your picture's own aspect ratio, so nothing gets cropped or stretched.
Pick a preset, or set it to custom and use your own width and height.
How large the overall resolution is. Set it lower for faster generation.
Reference Boost for image 1. 1.0 is standard, but I've noticed it locks facial expressions. Lower = less attention to the character.

steps.title: Image 2 🖼️ & 🙂 Head Swap
steps.text:
A second image, as a reference or as the face for a head swap. Turn it on with the Image 2 switch in User Settings.

⚠️ For a head swap, Remove Background should be on. Use a clean face reference: a headshot is best.

settings.why: As a reference: remove the background unless there is no subject. For a head swap: a clean headshot.
Reference Boost for image 2. 1 for both images works pretty well. For a head swap, set this all the way to 4 and lower the main one to 1.

steps.title: ⚙️ User Settings
steps.text: Prompt, switches, LoRA, seed and steps. This is the part you touch every run.

settings.why: Use a simple prompt: "Change her outfit to a red dress", "Put the outfit from image 2 on the woman in image 1". Leave it blank for a head swap.
Turn this on with the Head Swap switch. It will always be hit or miss, so try several different seeds 🌱
The Krea 2 identity edit LoRA. You will need to download this. The link is in the main notes.
Pick your model family. The Optimizer sets up the rest and picks the speed-ups.
I always use a fixed seed, so I can adjust things without it regenerating. Hit "New Fixed Random" when you want a change.
Anywhere between 8 and 10. It really differs between models.

steps.title: Detailer 🩹
steps.text:
Finds the face with SAM 3, redraws it at full detail and blends it back in. Runs before the upscale, on the small picture, where it's fast and sees the whole face.

⚠️ Do not use "detailed realistic skin". In Krea 2 that means "Hey! Make giant pores and blotches!!"

settings.why: "Face". Add :1 (Face:1) for only the biggest face.
0.3 to 0.35. Higher starts adding blotches and freckles, then redraws a different face.
On. Matches the redrawn face's color back to the picture so you don't get that washed out look.

steps.title: Upscaler ⬆️
steps.text:
LC VOSR2 Upscale. Built for speed and low VRAM: it sharpens and adds fine detail without redrawing the picture.

👋🏼 The first run downloads the weights (about 6.5 GB) into models/vosr2. This takes a few minutes.

settings.why: 1.5x to 3x needs about 5 GB, so it can almost run on a 🥔.

steps.title: 🎨 Post Processing
steps.text:
Color, sharpening, LUT and Natural Look. Turn each one on or off in the panel.

🛑 I HIGHLY suggest you fix the seed, run the pic, then don't mess with anything before this so it doesn't reprocess.

settings.why: Color Match: matches colors to a reference image. adain is the most stable.
Sharpen Pro: super important node. Adds "pop" without the cardboard cut-out look.
0.3 to 0.7 is often nicer than 1.0. Free LUTs at freshluts.com.
Takes the AI look out without making it dull. 0.3 to 0.6 for most renders.
How much orange or plastic skin gets calmed. 0 = skin untouched.
adds a time or date in your choice of format. Set to none if not wanted
leave on if you wanna give me props
